worldFact.locationContext: Pōrangahau, Hawke's Bay · North Island, New Zealand
worldFact.fact: A grassy hill near Pōrangahau holds the Guinness title for the world's longest place name: an 85-letter Māori name beginning Taumatawhakatangihanga. Roughly translated, it means 'the summit where Tamatea, the man with the big knees, the slider, climber of mountains', the land-swallowing traveller, played his nose flute to his loved one.

photo.alt: An uncharacteristic dump of snow over the Duchy brought, predictably, travel chaos on 18 Jan 1985; Britain's all weather naval air station (Culdrose) was closed because....no one could get on to the base to fly the all weather aircraft!! BR quietly got on with life and the (from memory) 08:45 Penmere to Truro ran on time, permitting my wife to get to work at City Hospital almost on time. For the record Class 118 DMU Set P464 consisting of 51306 and 51321 depart from Penmere Halt for Truro. Thanks to www.railcar.co.uk for the vehicle numbers - not sure where the centre car 59473 was)
